What is recursion? Show a recursive Fibonacci with memoization in Python and explain why memoization helps.

message.content:
# Recursion

Recursion is when a function calls itself to solve a problem by breaking it into smaller subproblems of the same type.

## Recursive Fibonacci with Memoization

```python
from functools import lru_cache

# Method 1: Using functools.lru_cache (Pythonic)
@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def fib_cached(n):
    if n <= 1:
        return n
    return fib_cached(n - 1) + fib_cached(n - 2)

# Method 2: Manual memoization (shows the concept)
def fib_manual_memo(n, memo={}):
    if n in memo:
        return memo[n]
    if n <= 1:
        return n
    memo[n] = fib_manual_memo(n - 1, memo) + fib_manual_memo(n - 2, memo)
    return memo[n]

# Without memoization (exponential time complexity)
def fib_naive(n):
    if n <= 1:
        return n
    return fib_naive(n - 1) + fib_naive(n - 2)
```

## Why Memoization Helps

```
fib(5) without memoization:
                         fib(5)
                        /      \
                   fib(4)      fib(3)
                  /     \      /     \
              fib(3) fib(2) fib(2) fib(1)
              /   \
          fib(2) fib(1)

→ 15 function calls for fib(5) — exponential O(2^n)

fib(5) with memoization:
fib(5) → fib(4) → fib(3) → fib(2) → fib(1)
→ 5 function calls — linear O(n)
```

| Approach | Time | Space | Calls for fib(20) |
|----------|------|-------|-------------------|
| Naive | O(2ⁿ) | O(n) | 21,891 |
| Memoized | O(n) | O
